title.narrative: Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Corridors 2, 5, and 6 (Dushanbe-Kurgonteppa) Road Project

description.narrative: The project will improve the connectivity between the capital Dushanbe and Kurgonteppa, which are two major cities and economic hubs in Tajikistan. The road is a strategic north-south link, and one of the most heavily traveled roads in the country, as well as the confluence of CAREC corridors 2, 5, and 6. The project will upgrade an approximately 33-kilometer (km) road section between Dushanbe and Chashmasoron, improve facilities and safety along and in the vicinity of this road section, strengthen the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Transport (MOT), and complete procurement readiness for the next section of the road to be improved.

Output: Improved road conditions, facilities, and safety along, and in the vicinity of the project road Indicator: About 73 km of road reconstructed with 100 km/h typical standard speed design and an average international roughness index of less than 2 m/km (2016 baseline: 5 m/km) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Original Project: Main civil works contract was awarded in September 2017. Works commenced in October 2017. The road was officially opened by the President of Tajikistan and ADB on 29 October 2021. On 30 December 2020, ADB approved the first three variations which increased the total contract price by $4.2 million from $47.46 million to $51.68 million (of which ADB's share of the increase is $3.4 million and OPEC Fund's share is $0.81 million). On 6 May 2022 ADB approved Variations 4&5 for increase of the contract amount by $13.mln and extension of completion date until 30 April 2022. All activities under the original project have been completed. Loan 3451 was financially closed on 21 February 2023. G0509 was also financially closed. However, bridge no. 2 (Km4+877, Kofarnigon river) is incomplete and expected remaining works will be covered by the government and completed in Q3 2024. G0510 was financially closed on 23 August 2023.
Additional Financing: Civil works contract was awarded on 26 July 2018 and have been completed on 31 March 2023. Public Traffic has been moving on the completed 4-lane asphalt road since November 2021. On 6 February 2023, civil works contract price of $62,75 million was increased for the remaining minor works. Physical progress is 100%. Data Source: Project progress reports and PCR from MOT and PMCSC

Output: Improved road conditions, facilities, and safety along, and in the vicinity of the project road Indicator: At least 1 health facility and 2 schools in the vicinity of the project road connected to solar power backup solutions Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Completed in 2023 Data Source: Project progress reports and PCR from MOT and PMCSC

Output: Safety on selected priority sections of the national highway network improved Indicator: Safety improved on at least 3 priority sections or black spots across the national highway network (2017 baseline: preconstruction road safety audits) Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Completed.
On 24 Feb 2021, the Government submitted the revised report for Black Spot Program (Road Safety Improvements). The Ministry of Transport (MOT) has fully considered and accepted all ADB recommendations. Accordingly, ADB approved the report which covers four procurement packages. All four packages have been awarded and signed.
These are:
(i) Ayni-Panjanket - Dushanbe-Tursonzoda Road safety Improvements. Contract (ICB/CP-05) was awarded and signed on 2 June 2022. Works were completed in September 2023.
(ii) Dushanbe-Vahdat Road Safety Improvements (CP-06), awarded and signed on 16 August 2021. Works were completed in October 2022.
(iii) Dushanbe-Kulob Road Safety Improvements (CP-07) awarded and signed on 9 March 2022. Works were completed in June 2023.
(iv) Dushanbe-Khujand Road Safety Improvements (istaravshan city passage) (CP-08), awarded and signed on 30 December 2021. Works were completed in November 2022.
On 31 October 2022, the Government submitted to ADB new report on Additional Proposed Improvement of Road Safety on Selected Priority Sections of National Highway Network. Based on that report procurement of two additional safety packages has been approved (CP-09 and CP-10).
(v) CP-09: Road Safety Improvement at CAREC Corridor 3 (Dushanbe-Uzbekistan border road) Km0 to Km5 and connecting road. The bidding document was approved on 1 March 2023 and IFB was published on 7 March 2023. Contract was awarded on 14 June 2023.The works are completed
(vi) CP-10: Road Safety Improvement at Asian Highway 66 (Dushanbe-Dangara- Kulob road) Km99 to Km107 and its connecting Kangurt-Baljuvon-Khovaling road. The bidding document was approved on 1 March 2023 and IFB was published on 7 March 2023. Contract was awarded on 14 June 2023. The works are completed.
(vii) CP-11/2023: Road safety improvement at Asian Highway 66 (km 23 - 87 from Vahdat city) and CAREC Corridors 2, 5, 6 (Dushanbe - Kurgonteppa Road km 16 - 83). On 16 August 2024, ADB approved the award of the contract which was completed by the project closure. Data Source: Road safety audit reports, project progress reports, and PCR from MOT and PMCSC.

In March 2020 ADB approved minor change in project scope for project preparation of new road project comprising three road sections: i) Temurmalik-Kholbug-Kangort (59km); ii) Dangara-Korgonteppa (Bokhtar) (69km); iii) Dangara-Gulistan (52km). There was variation to the contract for Project Management and Construction Supervision Consultant Contract (Kocks Engineers).
Hence, the output focuses on the road feasibility and design preparation for Road Network Sustainability Project (Grant 0752-TAJ) and its Additional Financing (Grant 0859-TAJ). The works included design for three road sections: (i) Hulbuk-Temurmalik-Kangurt road (G0752): the civil works contract has been awarded on 30 August 2021; (ii) Dangara-Okmazor-Bokhtar: the civil works contracts for Dangara-Okmazor road section (G0752) was awarded on 17 April 2022, and for Okmazor-Levakant and Levakant-Bokhtar road sections (G0859) on 17 November 2022; and (iii) Dangara-Guliston: detailed design has been completed by February 2022.
